basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 6.' and it opens 'Vers. 6. Vidit igitur mulier quod bonum esset lignum ad vescendum. Hic aperte ostenditur'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 6. Vidit igitur mulier quod bonum esset lignum ad vescendum. Hic aperte ostenditur mulier inexcusabilis esse. Licuit enim ei sub tali deliberatione | dolos advertere inimici. Consideravit enim pulchritudinem ligni et quia suave esset ad manducandum. Dedit viro suo. Non quidem dicitur, quod suaserit ei ut manducaret, sed in hoc quod dicitur: dedit, intelligitur quia suasit ad comedendum, quanquam non esset opus ut suaderet, quia, cum vidit eam comedisse et minime mori, ipse quoque securus comedit.
